page: Google Cloud Platform ct5lp-hightpu-1t is an accelerator-driven virtual machine within the TPU Machines product line, specifically provisioned for machine learning inference and distributed training tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 24 dedicated vCPUs alongside 48.0 GB of system memory. This yields a compute-dense 2.0 GB per core ratio, prioritizing processing power and execution throughput for workloads that offload heavy linear algebra routines to dedicated co-processors.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by a single Google TPU v5e chip containing 16 GB of dedicated high-bandwidth VRAM. The TPU architecture is purpose-built to accelerate neural network operations, including matrix multiplications and vector calculations, relieving the host x86 CPUs from processing primary tensor pipelines. This makes the configuration effective for serving transformer architectures, computer vision models, and mid-sized language models within the constraints of the 16 GB accelerator memory limit.

Infrastructure tradeoffs center on storage and networking provisions. The ct5lp-hightpu-1t includes no local storage volumes, requiring external persistent disk solutions to be mounted over the network for OS bootstrapping and data storage. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, favoring private cluster architectures and internal VPC deployments. From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the tight 2:1 memory-to-core ratio keeps host resource overhead low, aligning operational costs tightly with the utilization of the single TPU v5e unit for continuous inference and model evaluation workflows.
description: Google Cloud Platform ct5lp-hightpu-1t is an accelerator-optimized machine type within the TPU Machines family, designed for specialized machine learning training and inference workloads. The instance is powered by 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs paired with 48 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Computational acceleration is delivered by a single integrated Google TPU v5e processor equipped with 16 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. The instance does not feature local storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached persistent storage volumes for operating system disks and dataset staging. Operating without complimentary public IPv4 addressing, network access is typically managed via private networking or dedicated cloud gateways. With its lean memory-to-core allocation and dedicated hardware tensor processing capabilities, the ct5lp-hightpu-1t provides an efficient resource footprint for medium-scale deep learning model deployment, matrix-intensive mathematical computation, and continuous model evaluation pipelines.
